component.name: AC3SPDIF
component.summary: Dolby Digital Live and DTS Connect for Linux

description.p: AC3SPDIF captures all system audio, encodes it to AC-3 (Dolby Digital) or DTS in real time, and bitstreams the result out an S/PDIF or HDMI interface as an IEC 61937 data burst, so a receiver decodes 5.1 itself instead of being handed stereo PCM. It is what sound cards on other platforms call Dolby Digital Live or DTS Connect.

A virtual PipeWire sink becomes the system output; whatever plays into it is encoded in-process with ffmpeg's libraries and sent as a native passthrough stream to the digital output, or straight to the ALSA device for the lowest latency. The tray app shows buffer, drift and underrun figures live, with per-channel meters and a latency slider; the command line does the same with no UI and can run as a background service from login.

ul.li: AC-3 at up to 640 kb/s and DTS at up to 1536 kb/s, 5.1 or stereo
Native PipeWire passthrough or direct ALSA transport
Clock drift correction so two independent audio clocks stay in step
A self-test tone per channel to verify the receiver end

description.p: First release: AC-3 and DTS encoding, PipeWire passthrough and direct ALSA transports, tray app and command line.
